# Expert report — Referral & partnership channel design (incl. partner-as-customer trade)

# Referral & Partnership Channels for SMD — Applied Playbook

## 1. The current playbook, as it applies to SMD

The 2025 B2B referral consensus is narrow and unglamorous: **start with a referral program because it is the lowest-friction, lowest-cost partner motion** — a simple agreement, a tracking link, a payout mechanism — and within ~90 days you learn which partner types actually send qualified leads ([Introw](https://www.introw.io/blog/how-to-build-a-channel-partner-program)). For consulting-style B2B, the recommended incentive is a flat closed-deal payout (external benchmark: **$300–$500**) or a multi-step reward that pays at qualified-lead and again at close ([Commsor](https://www.commsor.com/post/b2b-referral-program-incentives)).

Here is the problem that generic playbook ignores and that dominates SMD's situation: **the exact partners SMD wants — CPAs, attorneys, insurance brokers — are largely barred from taking a cash referral fee.**

- **Attorneys:** ABA Model Rule 7.2(b) prohibits giving "anything of value" for recommending a lawyer's services, and Rule 5.4(a) bars fee-sharing with non-lawyers. Only nominal/token gifts are allowed ([ABA](https://www.americanbar.org/groups/professional_responsibility/publications/model_rules_of_professional_conduct/rule_7_2_advertising/comment_on_rule_7_2/)). A lawyer cannot take a commission for sending Scott a client, and Scott cannot take a cut of legal fees.
- **CPAs:** AICPA §1.510 permits referral fees only for **non-attest** clients and only with **written disclosure acknowledged by the client**; for any audit/review/compilation client a referral fee is **flatly prohibited, disclosure or not** ([AICPA](https://us.aicpa.org/interestareas/personalfinancialplanning/resources/practicecenter/professionalresponsibilities/commissionsreferralfees)).
- **Insurance brokers:** anti-rebating statutes (NAIC Model #880) make brokers culturally allergic to "consideration for inducement," even though paying an unlicensed party for a non-insurance referral is usually permissible if not conditioned on a policy sale ([IIAT](https://www.iiat.org/agency-operations/insurance-laws-regulations/insurance-laws-regulations-sales-marketing/rebating-and-referral-fees)).
- **Bookkeepers, fractional CFOs, commercial bankers:** materially less regulated; cash referral fees are generally fine. These are the partners where a conventional incentive works.

**This is exactly why Scott's "partner-as-customer trade" is the right instinct.** It routes value as a _product relationship_ rather than a _payment for referral_, sidestepping the compliance wall for the regulated half of the partner list — and it does something a check never could: it makes the partner a daily user and live reference.

## 2. Concrete tactics

**The flagship move — place an Operator inside the partner's own firm.** SMD already has packs for law, accounting, RIA, insurance, mortgage, and title. Onboard a friendly CPA or law firm as a real Operator customer (founding/beta terms). Three compounding effects: (a) the partner experiences the product, so referrals are sincere, not transactional; (b) Scott gets a working case study in the partner's vertical, which de-risks the _next_ pack sale; (c) the partner's office becomes a showroom — "the same kind of system running in my office" is the warmest possible proof point.

**Structure the trade as a genuine commercial relationship, not a bribe.** A free Operator given _expressly in exchange for referrals_ is "a thing of value for recommending services" and re-creates the very ethics problem you're trying to avoid. Keep the two threads separate: the partner is a real (founding-rate) customer of the Operator; referrals flow because they're a happy user and a peer, documented as a non-contingent introduction. For CPAs/attorneys specifically, default to **reciprocity, not cash** — Scott refers operationally-painful clients _to_ them; they introduce clients to SMD. Mutual referral between professionals is the compliant norm.

**Tactical list:**

- Lead with the **least-regulated partners first**: bookkeepers and fractional CFOs see SMB operational mess daily, own the owner's trust, and _can_ take a standard $300–$500 closed-deal payout. Fastest path to a live referral.
- For CPAs/attorneys, offer **reciprocal referral + a founding Operator placement**, never a commission. Hand each a one-page, plain-English note on why you don't pay them (it protects _their_ license) — that candor builds trust.
- **Anchor in existing local rooms**: BNI, EO Arizona, Vistage, Phoenix chambers (Decisions #21–25 already name these). Partnerships here are face-to-face, which fits the Phase-1 in-person consulting default.
- **Co-host a working session** with one partner ("Operations teardown for [partner]'s top clients") — the partner convenes their book, Scott runs assessments. The Operator placement is the demo.
- **Make the partner's intro trivial**: give them a forwardable two-line email and a single link to `/book`. The harder you make it, the less it happens.

## 3. Benchmarks (external — not SMD data)

- Warm intro/referral leads convert at **~15–25%** vs **1.5–3%** for cold lists; warm leads convert **5–10×** cold ([Ivris](https://ivristech.com/warm-vs-cold-lead-conversion-multiplier/), [Rhythm of Business](https://www.rhythmof.business/blog/warm-referral-conversion-gap/)).
- Partner referrals = **~10% of pipeline but ~31% of revenue**; warm referrals close **~38% faster** ([Trackier](https://trackier.com/b2b-referral-program-trackiers-top-7-tips-for-you/), [Rhythm of Business](https://www.rhythmof.business/resources/warm-referral-research/)).
- Typical B2B closed-deal referral incentive: **$300–$500 flat**, or staged across the funnel ([Commsor](https://www.commsor.com/post/b2b-referral-program-incentives)).
- 2025 Medicare insurance referral fees are capped at **$100** — a useful reference for how tight regulated-industry referral economics are ([NJCPA/IIAT context](https://www.iiat.org/agency-operations/insurance-laws-regulations/insurance-laws-regulations-sales-marketing/rebating-and-referral-fees)).

## 4. Honest fit assessment

**Speed to first lead: slow.** This channel does **not** relieve the "produce leads NOW" pressure. It requires trust-building before a single intro arrives, and the partner-as-customer trade requires onboarding a live Operator first. The near-term lead problem is better solved by the **~100 enriched, already-drafted outreach messages sitting unsent** in the CRM. Referral is the _compounding_ play layered behind that, not the emergency valve.

**Lead quality/warmth: the best you can get.** A referred owner arrives pre-trusted; the partner has already validated the pain from the inside (a bookkeeper _sees_ the spreadsheet chaos). This is the warmest channel SMD has and the one most aligned with a buyer "whose operational pain is invisible from the outside" — the partner makes the invisible visible for you.

**What makes it fail:**

1. **Treating it as an incentive program instead of a relationship.** Pre-launch with zero case studies, no partner will risk their client relationship on an unproven vendor for $400. Referrals follow _demonstrated_ results, not bounties.
2. **A compliance misstep that burns the partner's license** — instantly fatal to the relationship and to word-of-mouth. The "no cash to regulated professionals" rule is non-negotiable.
3. **One-sided trade.** If Scott takes referrals but never reciprocates, the well dries up.
4. **No proof.** The partner-as-customer placement is precisely what breaks this logjam — it manufactures the first proof point.

**The honest summary:** high-warmth, high-conversion, slow-to-start, compounding. Run it _in parallel_ with the unsent-drafts campaign, not instead of it.

## 5. Phased ramp (sequence, not calendar)

- **Initial moves:** Pick **one** warm, friendly partner Scott already trusts — ideally a bookkeeper or a law firm matching an existing pack. Land a single Operator inside their firm as a founding customer. Draft the per-partner-type compliance note (lawyer / CPA / broker / bookkeeper). Add a `referral_partner` field to the admin CRM entity.
- **Early build:** Convert that one placement into a written mini-case study. Codify the trade terms and a one-page partner brief (what SMD is, who's a fit, the forwardable intro + `/book` link). Recruit a small handful of partners across the _less-regulated_ tier where reciprocity or a clean $300–$500 payout applies.
- **Maturing:** Formalize tiers (reciprocal-only for regulated professionals; paid-referral for unregulated). Stack partner-vertical case studies so each Operator placement de-risks the next pack. Introduce co-hosted assessment sessions and, only once volume justifies it, lightweight attribution tooling.

## 6. How a touched prospect reaches the assessment

The partner makes a warm, **non-contingent** introduction — a forwarded two-liner or an in-person "you should talk to Scott." The prospect lands on the **single front door, `/book`** (the one assessment entry; consulting and Operator are _outcomes_, not separate doors). Because they're referred, they skip cold skepticism and arrive ready for the Operator-led assessment interview. The partner's own running Operator is the referenceable proof — "I have one in my office" — which primes the report-and-human-close mechanic in ADR 0039. Attribution stays deliberately low-tech for a pre-launch venture: a "who referred you" field on `/book` plus the CRM partner tag. No PRM, no tracking-link infrastructure until there's volume to justify it.
